answer: An agent economy resists sybils with quadratic attestation weighting: an identity's epoch reward scales with the square root of the number of independent peers that verified its work. The ripple of one honest agent's work reaches many independent checkers, but a farm's fakes can only attest each other, so their shared attestors collapse to one weight. At dawn each epoch the attestor graph is re-randomized across the tundra of participants, preventing pre-arranged clusters. A thousand fakes earn little more than one identity, while bribing independent attestors costs the attacker per fake.
